title: Choose Vartifact's new visual world
question: Choose one complete direction for the whole website, or re-roll for a new set.

options.label: The Redline Atlas
options.lineage: architectural drawing sets, redline reviews, and translucent tracing overlays
options.thesis: Vartifact becomes a living drawing set where every article is a numbered detail in one authored body of work.
options.viewport: A full drawing sheet opens with an oversized Vartifact section mark, a strict title block, and recent articles plotted as numbered details across the grid.
options.risk: It can feel like an architecture portfolio if the article language and personal voice are not kept dominant.

raised.raise: Linked geometry: navigation, article indexes, and reading notes share one coordinate system instead of becoming separate widgets.
Persistent place: the last-read article and current reading position return as a clear physical mark.
Claim-proof discipline: every article teaser pairs its title with a concrete description or visible artifact.

options.label: The Contact Sheet Reading Room
options.lineage: darkroom contact sheets, grease-pencil selects, and photographic proof tables
options.thesis: Articles become frames in a personal proof sheet, with one chosen thought enlarged for close reading.
options.viewport: A near-black proof table fills the screen; recent articles sit as numbered frames while one selected story expands into a bright reading window.
options.risk: This familiar photography language needs enough real cover imagery to avoid becoming decorative empty frames.

options.label: The Daylight Section
options.thesis: Reading unfolds as a daylit section, with each article occupying a room along a moving band of light.
options.viewport: The first screen is one continuous building section; the newest article sits in the brightest room while older writing recedes into cooler shadow.
options.case: It gives the archive a memorable reading journey, but the spatial metaphor is less direct for developers than a drawing set.
options.risk: The atmosphere can overpower article scanning if light and annotation are not kept functional.

options.label: The Friend's Technical Zine
options.lineage: hand-drawn explainer zines and annotated code sketches
options.thesis: Hard ideas are taught like a friend sketching them beside you, with clear body text surrounded by authored marks and diagrams.
options.viewport: A bold hand-lettered Vartifact opens above three numbered article panels, with a small guide character pointing to the latest idea.
options.case: It is personal and welcoming for difficult technical topics, but playful marks may weaken long-form calm if used everywhere.
options.risk: Without real hand-authored diagrams, the style can look artificial or childish.

options.label: The Article Concourse
options.lineage: international airport wayfinding and monumental gate signs
options.thesis: Every visit becomes a clear chain of reading decisions, with articles treated as destinations rather than cards.
options.viewport: A saturated yellow sign band names Vartifact and points toward Writing, About, and Contact; the latest article number fills the lower concourse.
options.case: It delivers exceptional wayfinding and mobile clarity, but it risks making a personal blog feel institutional.
options.risk: The yellow system must remain readable and personal across long articles, not only navigation screens.

options.label: The Deployable Article Sheet
options.thesis: The archive opens from a compact packet into one linked field of articles.
options.viewport: A folded article packet begins opening across the first screen.
options.case: The deployment is memorable, but it makes basic reading and navigation harder to understand.
options.kept: Its linked geometry raised the assigned direction into one connected coordinate system.
options.risk: The fold metaphor can become a visual puzzle instead of a reading tool.

options.label: The Cutting Bench
options.lineage: film work prints, select rails, and pinned trims
options.thesis: Articles run through a fixed editing rail while saved and deferred pieces hang below.
options.viewport: A horizontal rail scrubs through article frames and stops at the latest selection.
options.case: It supports selection and return state, but long articles do not naturally belong on a cutting bench.
options.kept: Its persistent place marker became a durable last-read and reading-position cue.
options.risk: Horizontal scrubbing can fight expected reading behavior.

options.label: The Monochrome Proof
options.lineage: neutral product marketing with claim-and-proof pairs
options.thesis: Every article promise is immediately paired with visible proof or a concrete excerpt.
options.viewport: A simple introduction sits beside one large proof frame for the newest article.
options.case: It is clear, but it treats a personal article archive like software marketing.
options.kept: Its claim-proof discipline strengthened every article teaser.
options.risk: It would be polished but too close to a generic professional website.

canonCard.label: The Contemporary Reading Blog
canonCard.thesis: A familiar article-first personal blog, executed with excellent typography and spacing.
canonCard.viewport: A clear author introduction leads into a conventional list of recent articles and social links.
canonCard.risk: It is easy to use, but it may look like many other well-made personal blogs.
